title: The Nile River
text: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeastern Africa, generally regarded as the longest river in the world at approximately 6,650 km, though this is disputed by some measurements of the Amazon. It flows from its sources in the African Great Lakes region through Uganda, Sudan, and Egypt before draining into the Mediterranean Sea. The Nile has two major tributaries: the White Nile and the Blue Nile. Ancient Egyptian civilization developed along the Nile's banks, dependent on its annual flooding to deposit fertile silt on the fields. Today, the Nile provides water for drinking and irrigation for approximately 300 million people across eleven countries.
